$comment: USPA's competition categories, transcribed from the rulebook cited in `provenance`.
Curated by hand rather than parsed, and that is a decision, not a shortcut. The
only machine-readable form of these figures is a 68-page PDF whose layout changes
every year; a layout-sensitive parser that half-succeeds would publish a ladder
with a class missing from the middle, and nothing downstream can tell that from a
federation that removed one. Transcription fails visibly in review instead.
What keeps it honest is `provenance.retrievedAt` and the invariants the adapter
checks -- see `packages/ingestion/src/sources/uspa-categories.ts`. What is still
missing is upstream change detection, so that a rulebook revision announces itself
rather than waiting for someone to notice.
Only figures belong here. Labels are derived, so a boundary and its caption cannot
disagree. Identifiers are not derived, because they key records and standards and
must survive a boundary moving.

ageDivisions.label: USPA age divisions
$comment: `age-on-meet-date` is the rulebook's own basis: Item 1.2.1 requires the lifter to
have attained the age on the day of the competition. Federations that read age
across the calendar year instead put a December-born lifter in a different
division for most of the year, which is why the basis travels with the set.
The rulebook prints five separate divisions under the single word Junior and
distinguishes them only by the range beside it. The range is therefore part of
the name here, not a gloss added by this project -- five options reading Junior
would be unusable, and the adapter refuses duplicate labels so that going back
to one is a build failure rather than a screen nobody can answer.
`junior-15-19` overlaps `junior-13-15`, `junior-16-17` and `junior-18-19`, and that
is not a transcription error. The federation contests it and keeps records under it
-- 1,126 of them across IPL world, Kansas and Ohio, the most recent set in June
2026. Divisions overlap by design anyway; an Open lifter of 45 is eligible for a
Masters division at the same meet. Leaving it out to keep the ladder tidy would
drop every one of those records on the floor, including current world records, and
the lifter would see an empty category rather than a missing one.

$comment:levels: The levels the federation keeps records at, and the regions each is divided into.
These are here rather than in the records document because a lifter picks a level
and a region *before* anything knows which record file to fetch -- records are
partitioned on exactly those two axes. A vocabulary published inside a partition
could only be read by somebody who already knew which partition they wanted.
The state list is enumerated from the federation's own published record pages, not
from the fifty states: a state with no affiliate keeps no records, and inventing a
level for one would offer a lifter a category that cannot be answered. Guam links a
record page and every one of its tables answered 503 at the last crawl, so it is
recorded as an absence in the records document rather than as a region here -- a
region with no records is indistinguishable on screen from one whose records failed
`national` and `ipl-world` carry no regions. There is one national record, not one
per state, and the empty list says so where a missing field could not.
$comment:disciplines: The events the federation contests, and which lifts each holds records in.
Carried rather than inferred from the name. "Deadlift Only" is a caption, and a
project that read the caption would be guessing in the federation's language about
Without this axis two records collide: the best raw bench by an open man at a
full-power meet and the best at a bench-only meet are two records the federation
keeps separately, and on the published corpus a scope without the discipline makes
twenty thousand rows land on the same identity -- which surfaces to a lifter as no
record at all, because the lookup refuses to choose between two.
A single-lift meet has no total. A bench-only book that listed one would be
reporting a lifter's bench as their three-lift total.
